title: Don Norman Coins 'User Experience' at Apple (mid-1990s)
explainer: The phrase 'user experience' was brought into wider use by Don Norman, who held the title of User Experience Architect at Apple and first presented the term publicly at a 1995 conference. He later said he coined it because 'human interface' and 'usability' felt too narrow, covering only the screen interaction rather than everything a person encounters - packaging, first setup, documentation - which is exactly the broader scope UX/UI work covers today, beyond just visual screen design.

title: Doug Engelbart's 1968 Demo and the Origin of Direct Manipulation
explainer: On December 9, 1968, Douglas Engelbart's team at Stanford Research Institute gave a 90-minute public demonstration - later nicknamed 'The Mother of All Demos' - that introduced the computer mouse alongside windows, hypertext links, and real-time collaborative editing, all built to let one person interact with a screen directly rather than through punch cards or typed commands. That demo is the ancestor of the pointer-driven, direct-manipulation interface model that essentially all modern UI design, from desktop windows to touchscreens, still builds on.
